def route_message(
    message: str,
    model: BaseChatModel,
    *,
    call: TraceCall | None = None,
) -> RouteOut | None:
    """One structured call; ``None`` means the answer did not match ``RouteOut``."""
    answer = ask(
        model,
        RouteOut,
        prompt_messages(SYSTEM_PROMPT, message),
        task=TASK,
        tool=TOOL,
        prompt_version=PROMPT_VERSION,
        call=call,
    )
    return answer.parsed if answer.schema_valid else None

examples.answer: Keep the provider API key in the repository-root `.env` file, which is gitignored. In `config/providers.toml`, reference it with an `env:NAME` pointer (for example, `env:OPENAI_API_KEY`) rather than pasting the key. The project resolves that named environment variable when needed.

passages.label: connect-provider · passage 0
passages.text: Connect a provider with BYOK and wam doctor Every model call in this project goes through a Connection: a small record that says where to call, which wire protocol to speak, and which environment variable holds the key. You bring your own key (BYOK). Keys live only in the gitignored .env file at the repository root and are referenced from configuration as env:NAME pointers, never pasted into code, logs, traces, or recordings.

passages.label: connect-provider · passage 2
passages.text: Presets and the credential rule The gateway preset used for the benchmark is exposed as four connections sharing one key, one per API format, beside the standard openai, anthropic, gemini, openrouter, local-openai-compatible, and custom presets. resolve_credential reads the named variable at call time and returns the key value, or None for keyless connections. Only the credentials module and the live benchmark runner may touch the environment for a secret;

examples.question: Where should I keep my provider API key, and how do I point the project configuration at it without pasting the secret anywhere?

examples.answer: The four connection protocols and the provider-side APIs they speak are: `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE` — Chat Completions endpoints; `OPENAI_RESPONSES` — the Responses API; `ANTHROPIC` — the Messages API; and `GEMINI` — the Google Generative Language API.

passages.label: connect-provider · passage 1
passages.text: How a connection is described A connection has an id, a provider label, a protocol, a base URL, and a credential reference. The protocol is one of four fixed values: OPENAI_COMPATIBLE for Chat Completions endpoints, OPENAI_RESPONSES for the Responses API, ANTHROPIC for the Messages API, and GEMINI for the Google Generative Language API. The base URL never carries credentials; a URL with an @ before its first path slash is rejected by the contracts.

examples.question: What are the four connection protocols in this project, and which provider-side API does each one speak?

examples.answer: For each configured connection, `wam doctor` shows its id, protocol, outcome, and latency in milliseconds. It can report these outcome values: `OK`, `CONFIG_INVALID`, `CREDENTIAL_MISSING`, `CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `ENDPOINT_UNREACHABLE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED`, or `UNKNOWN`.

passages.label: connect-provider · passage 3
passages.text: Checking what works with wam doctor Run wam doctor before spending anything. It probes every configured connection and prints one row per connection with its id, protocol, outcome, and latency in milliseconds. The outcome vocabulary is fixed: OK, CONFIG_INVALID, CREDENTIAL_MISSING, CREDENTIAL_REJECTED, ENDPOINT_UNREACHABLE, RATE_LIMITED, PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED, or UNKNOWN. Scripts and the runner switch on these values without guessing, and the detail field is scrubbed of headers and key material first.

entries: All seven models were reached through one gateway (OpenCode Go), each in its lab's own API format. Other providers' direct endpoints were tested only with mocks.
Four of the five before tools were written for this project. Only the tool-calling agent is adapted from real earlier code, and it is credited in THIRD_PARTY.md.
Tiers are mixed on purpose: Gemini 4 Argon is a flagship, the other six are small models. A flagship winning on quality is expected; the useful question is what the small models cost.
The datasets are public, so models may already know some test messages. All seven saw the same text, so the comparison is still like for like, but absolute scores may be optimistic.
The structured-reply sample is a subset of the routing sample, so the recorded answers are not independent questions.
The gateway did not send measured cost on every model. Where it did not, the committed price table is used, and the measured-versus-list gap is computed only over models that have both.
Results and prices are dated in the technical details below. A later price change is not reflected here.
The docs task was scored with an in-memory index built from the same guide and the same pinned embeddings as the pgvector store. Retrieval ids matched pgvector on every gold question.

recheck.lead: A benchmark result is about one model, at one moment, with one prompt and one set of settings. When any of those changes, re-test instead of trusting the old number. These are the exact commands from docs/recheck.md.

steps.body: A new model has no earlier answers, so a normal record run is enough: only the new model's calls are made. Then gate it against the committed run.

commands.text:
wam bench --mode record --models config/new-model.lock.toml \
  --tasks T-SCOPE --run-id new-model

commands.note: Then compare it with the committed run:

steps.title: A new model came out

steps.body: This is what re-check is for. It records fresh answers, never reuses a saved one, scores them, and gates them against the earlier run with the same model id on both sides.

commands.text:
wam recheck run \
  --models config/models.lock.toml \
  --tasks T-SCOPE \
  --against results/runs/live \
  --candidate gpt-6-luna \
  --run-id recheck-gpt-6-luna

steps.title: The same model id behaves differently

steps.body: Temperature, reasoning and the output allowance are recorded in the run manifest. A difference is refused unless you say it was intended; then the gate returns its normal verdict plus a WARN line naming every difference.

commands.text:
wam recheck run \
  --models config/models.lock.toml \
  --tasks T-SCOPE \
  --against results/runs/live \
  --candidate gpt-6-luna \
  --accept-settings-mismatch \
  --run-id recheck-gpt-6-luna-warm
